payload.gaps:
Three new entries, plus the standing ones carried forward.

NEW, and the honest one first: se.raid-closed-iteration-detail-unreadable (issue, agent). R12's check proves the grant index FILE survives the filter - it does not prove that projectState or the board actually lists a closed iteration from it. So 'the archive stays listable' currently rests on the index existing rather than on a reader using it, and a closed iteration could be listable in principle while absent from the board in practice. i5e closes this by rewiring the readers to resolve archived iterations from tags; until then the check is to look at the board after a close.

se.raid-mid-merge-crash-window (risk, agent) - the residue flagged at the architecture gate, now in the register rather than only in a gate brief: between merge --no-commit and the commit, trunk's working copy is mid-merge. HEAD does not move and no refusal is skipped, so nothing recorded is lost, but a crash there leaves a working copy needing a human abort. The mitigation if it ever bites is to detect a pending MERGE_HEAD at the next close and refuse.

se.raid-engine-iteration-cannot-self-demonstrate (assumption, agent) - a bootstrap fact worth naming because it is easy to misread: an iteration that changes the engine cannot demonstrate its change on its own ship, since the running engine predates it. i5d's own close therefore runs under the pre-split engine unless deliberately driven from the built code, and the FOLLOWING iteration's close is the first honest demonstration.

CARRIED, still open: se.raid-tags-not-pushed (risk, OWNER, high - the push must carry tags or the remote holds claims with no record); se.raid-shallow-clone-loses-record (risk, agent); se.raid-audit-frequency-shifts-the-balance (assumption, owner); se.raid-battery-windows-parallel-flake (risk, agent - mitigated by the serial battery, the deeper root still owed); se.raid-phone-live-pairing (risk, owner, untouched here).

CLOSED BY THIS ITERATION: se.raid-worktree-provisioning-incomplete - a provisioned worktree now installs its own toolchain and warns when it would fork from a state that does not match the running engine.
